Definition: A tiered documentation architecture specifying six layers of threshold documentation for clinical AI governance records.
A governance threshold where failure can directly cause patient harm. Requires all six TJS documentation layers.
A governance threshold governing operational performance where failure does not directly cause irreversible patient harm. Requires three core TJS layers.
When a threshold cannot be clearly classified as Primary Safety or Secondary Operational, Primary Safety requirements apply by default.
Failure mechanism where the metric bears only an indirect causal relationship to the harm it purports to control.
Failure mechanism where uniform thresholds are applied across settings with materially different risk profiles.
Failure mechanism where multi-metric governance systems assess thresholds independently; compound failure modes remain undetected.
Failure mechanism where hard cutoffs create incentives to optimise the metric rather than improve underlying safety.
Failure mechanism where quantifiable performance metrics crowd out harder-to-measure sociotechnical risks.
Failure mechanism where a threshold justified at initial audit loses validity as population, data pipeline, or system version changes.
TJS Layer 1. Document the specific harm the threshold constrains and the causal pathway.
TJS Layer 2. Specify clinical setting, patient population, and acuity level.
TJS Layer 3. Empirical, simulation, or expert-consensus evidence supporting the numeric value.
TJS Layer 4. Evaluate governance outcomes as threshold varies; identify cliff-edge regions.
TJS Layer 5. Assess whether the threshold can be cleared through metric manipulation.
TJS Layer 6. Prespecify conditions triggering threshold re-evaluation.
